q-181555.name: Question 1
q-181555.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set $B$ is the number of elements in $B.$ 

Let's start by listing all the elements of $B:$

$$
1,\,2,\,3,\,4,\,5
$$

Note that only *unique* elements are counted. In other words, duplicate elements are *not* counted separately.

Since $B$ has $5$ elements, its cardinality is $|B|=\text{5}.$

q-1165.name: Question 3
q-1165.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set $T$ is the number of elements in $T.$ 

Let's start by listing all the elements of $T:$

$$
x,\,{x}^{2},\,{x}^{3},\,y,\,{x,{x}^{2}},\,{x,y,y}
$$

Note that ${x,{x}^{2}}$ and ${x,y,y}$ each count as single elements of $T.$

Since $T$ has $6$ elements, the cardinality is $|T|=6.$

q-181572.name: Question 8
q-181572.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
-3\,322,\,-3\,311,\,-3\,300,\,…
$$

form an arithmetic sequence with a common difference $d=11:$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =11 \\  & =-3\,311-(-3\,322) \\  & =-3\,300-(-3\,311) \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our arithmetic sequence, denoted ${a}_{n},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-3\,322\,+(n-1)\cdot 11 \\  & =-3\,322+11n-11 \\  & =11n-3\,333.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={11n-3\,333:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N}\end{aligned}
$$

where $N\in N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}11N-3\,333 & =2\,332 \\ 11N & =5\,665 \\ N & =\frac{5\,665}{11} \\ N & =515\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A={11n-3\,333:n\in N,\,1\le n\le 515}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $515$ elements, we must have $|A|=515.$
